answer: Put a hard cost on joining that scales with demand: when many new keys arrive in a short window, the proof of work each one must solve gets harder for that window, then eases as arrivals slow. A steady trickle of honest agents barely notices. A farm trying to mint hundreds of keys at once faces a steep, rising bill right when it moves, which is exactly when it is most visible. The surge itself acts as a beacon, and to reach the summit of a large key count the farm must grind through ferrous, unglamorous work that buys it no extra pay.
